title: (Scripture Reading Exercise.)
author: B. H. Roberts
note: Fifth Year (final) of the Seventy's Course in Theology. Focuses on divine immanence, the Holy Spirit, and nature of God.

footnotes.text: "No man can say that Jesus is the Lord but by the Holy Ghost." I Cor. xii:3.
"Natural Law in the Spiritual World," pp. 91-94.

On this head the Prophet of the New Dispensation of the Gospel, Joseph Smith, has a fine passage: "If you wish to go where God is, you must be like God, or possess the principles which God possesses, for it we are not drawing towards God in principle, we are going from Him, and drawing towards the devil. . . . A man is saved no faster than he gets knowledge, for if he does not get knowledge, he will be brought into captivity by some evil power in the other world, as evil spirits will have more knowledge, and consequently more power than many men who are on the earth. Hence it needs revelation to assist us, and give us knowledge of the things of God." (Minutes of April Conference, 1842. History of the Church, Vol. IV, p. 588.)
"Natural Law in the Spiritual World," pp. 293-6.
